title: Kirby Problem 1.14
exact_target: Which nonzero rational surgeries on every nontrivial knot have a fundamental group with a nonabelian representation into $\operatorname{SU}(2)$?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth nontrivial knot. For $r=p/q\in\mathbb Q$, with
$p,q$ coprime and $q>0$, write $S^3_r(K)$ for Dehn surgery along
$p\mu+q\lambda$, where $\mu$ is the meridian and $\lambda$ is the longitude
having zero linking number with $K$. Define
\[
\operatorname{SU}(2)=\{A\in M_2(\mathbb C):A^*A=I,\ \det A=1\}.
\]
A representation $\rho:\pi_1(S^3_r(K))\to\operatorname{SU}(2)$ has nonabelian
image if some two elements of its image do not commute.

Determine exactly the set
\[
\mathcal R=\{r\in\mathbb Q\setminus\{0\}:\text{ every nontrivial }K\subset S^3
\text{ admits such a nonabelian }\rho\}.
\]
The order of quantifiers matters: one slope must work for every nontrivial knot,
while the representation can depend on both slope and knot. For a slope outside
$\mathcal R$, a counterexample must have only abelian $\operatorname{SU}(2)$ images,
not simply fail a particular construction of representations. Replacing a knot
by its mirror reverses the surgery slope, so the classification is symmetric
under $r\mapsto-r$.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Which nonzero rational surgeries on every nontrivial knot have a fundamental group with a nonabelian representation into $\operatorname{SU}(2)$?
